Global Error Pause Behavior

Global Error Pause is a stand-alone interceptor behavior that conditionally blocks incoming pipeline candidates while a global Vault error is active.

This behavior operates exclusively in the Interceptor stage and does not require a controller to function. It determines whether an incoming candidate is admitted into the pipeline based solely on the presence of a global error signal.

When a global error is active, all incoming candidates are blocked and are not queued, delayed, or replayed. Blocked candidates are discarded and do not re-enter the pipeline automatically when the error is cleared. Once the global error is resolved, only newly incoming candidates are eligible for admission.

Global Error Pause does not transform state, buffer values, or perform validation. Its sole responsibility is to gate pipeline admission in response to global error conditions.

If replay of blocked candidates is required after a global error is cleared, the withReplayGlobalErrorController must be used explicitly. Replay behavior is not provided by the Global Error Pause behavior itself.

Diagram
Configuration

Global Error Pause introduces a conditional admission gate that prevents incoming state updates from entering the pipeline while a global Vault error is active. When an error is present, all incoming updates are immediately suppressed at the Interceptor stage.

This behavior does not introduce time-based windows or buffering. Admission is controlled entirely by the current global error state. As soon as the error condition is cleared, subsequent incoming updates are allowed to proceed through the pipeline without delay.

Global Error Pause is intended to protect pipeline integrity during unrecoverable or system-level failure states. It ensures that no new state mutations are processed while the Vault is in an error condition, preventing cascading failures, partial updates, or inconsistent state transitions.

This behavior does not accept configuration parameters and does not use the fluent interceptor API. It must be attached during FeatureCell instantiation.

FeatureCell Initialization

The Global Error Pause behavior is attached directly during FeatureCell definition and is not configured through a fluent API. This interceptor is registered once, at construction time, as part of the FeatureCell’s structural pipeline configuration.

Because this behavior gates pipeline admission based on global Vault error state, it must be present before any pipeline execution begins. Attaching it at definition time ensures that all incoming updates are consistently evaluated against global error conditions from the moment the FeatureCell is initialized.

This design ensures deterministic gating behavior and prevents runtime mutation of global error handling rules. The interceptor observes global Vault error signals and blocks incoming pipeline executions while an error is present, resuming normal operation automatically once the error condition is cleared.

Examples

withGlobalErrorPauseBehavior is a structural interceptor that must be attached when defining a FeatureCell. Unlike other interceptors, it is not registered through the fluent interceptor API and cannot be added dynamically after initialization.

This behavior blocks incoming pipeline executions whenever a global Vault error is present.

Example 1: Configure a FeatureCell with Global Error Pause

In this example, the FeatureCell is defined with a global error pause interceptor. While a global Vault error is active, all incoming state updates are blocked at the Interceptor stage. Once the error is cleared, pending updates are replayed automatically by the paired controller. 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault(),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService,
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: []
      },
      [
        // Attach the Global Error Pause interceptor at definition time
        withGlobalErrorPauseBehavior
      ],
      [
        // Additional add-on controllers
      ]
    )
  ]
};

@FeatureCell<Employee[][]>('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[][]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Attach the Global Error Pause interceptor at definition time
    withGlobalErrorPauseBehavior
  ],
  [
    // Additional add-on controllers
  ]
);

// Initialize the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Attach the Global Error Pause interceptor at definition time
    withGlobalErrorPauseBehavior
  ],
  [
    // Additional add-on controllers
  ]
);

// Initialize the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();`}}
